domains.desc: Compute, databases, storage and network choices

domains.name: Deploying solutions
domains.desc: VMs, GKE, Cloud Run, networking and IaC

lessons.summary: An organization can contain folders and projects. Projects are the main boundary for enabling APIs, tracking resources, quotas, IAM and billing association.
terms: Billing accounts fund projects; budgets alert but do not automatically cap spending
APIs often need to be enabled before use
lessons.connection: Think of a GCP project as the controlled workspace for a customer deployment. In your Azar work, separate projects isolate the tree-service app and admin agent.
lessons.example: A team needs to separate development from production and track spend. Use separate projects linked to billing accounts, assign least-privilege project roles, and configure budgets.
lessons.pitfall: A billing budget alert is not a hard shutdown or spending cap.
lessons.lab: Console → IAM & Admin → Manage Resources; inspect projects. Then Billing → Budgets & alerts. Avoid creating chargeable resources.

lessons.summary: IAM grants principals roles on resources. A service account is an identity used by applications and workloads. Prefer predefined roles with minimum permissions.
terms: Basic roles (Owner, Editor, Viewer) are broad
Service account impersonation and short-lived credentials are preferred over static keys
lessons.connection: Your Cloud Run scheduler and runtime service accounts are concrete examples: each identity gets only the permissions needed to invoke a service or read a secret.
lessons.example: A Cloud Run service needs Firestore access, but no broad project administration: attach a dedicated service account with the necessary data permissions.
lessons.pitfall: Giving Editor to a service account is usually excessive.
lessons.lab: Console → IAM & Admin → Service Accounts. Inspect an existing service account and its roles; avoid creating keys.

lessons.t: Compute Engine vs Cloud Run vs GKE
lessons.summary: Compute Engine runs VMs; Cloud Run runs containerized apps without managing servers; GKE manages Kubernetes clusters for orchestrated containers.
lessons.connection: Your deployed cloud-tam-portfolio and Azar applications use Cloud Run. Compare that with traditional on-prem workloads you supported at Prolexic and Akamai.
lessons.example: A stateless HTTP API packaged in a container, with variable traffic and minimal infrastructure administration, is a strong Cloud Run candidate.
lessons.pitfall: Do not choose GKE merely because an application uses containers.
lessons.lab: Console → Cloud Run → Services. Inspect revision, scaling and service identity settings in an existing service.

lessons.summary: A VPC is a global virtual network with regional subnets. Firewall rules control ingress/egress. Cloud NAT permits outbound internet access for eligible workloads without an external IP.
terms: Cloud NAT = outbound translation, not inbound exposure
Routes determine paths; firewall policies determine allowed traffic
lessons.connection: This is directly tied to your GRE/BGP/routing and firewall troubleshooting at Prolexic and Hybrid Networks; Cloud DNS maps to BlueCat DNS experience.
lessons.example: A private VM must download updates but should have no public IP. Use an appropriate route and Cloud NAT for outbound internet access.
lessons.pitfall: Cloud NAT is not an inbound load balancer or an inbound port-forwarding service.
lessons.lab: Console → VPC network → VPC networks, subnets, firewall rules. Identify one subnet region and the firewall rules affecting workloads.

lessons.summary: Cloud Storage stores objects in buckets; Cloud SQL provides managed relational databases; Firestore provides a document database; BigQuery is for analytics.
terms: Storage classes balance access patterns and retrieval costs
lessons.connection: Azar quotes/invoices stored in Firestore are document-oriented. Compare the app documents to structured SQL rows and use Cloud Storage for generated PDFs or uploaded files.
lessons.example: An application needs flexible JSON-like records and automatic scaling: Firestore may fit. Financial SQL transactions with relational constraints may fit Cloud SQL.
lessons.pitfall: BigQuery is not the standard replacement for a transactional application database.
lessons.lab: Console → Firestore → Databases; explore document collections. Console → Cloud Storage → Buckets; review storage-class choices.

lessons.summary: The Google Cloud CLI configures and manages cloud resources. Terraform describes desired infrastructure declaratively and reconciles it through a plan/apply workflow.
terms: gcloud config list = current CLI configuration
gcloud config set project PROJECT_ID = switch active project
terraform plan = preview changes; terraform apply = execute
lessons.connection: You already used gcloud run deploy and gcloud run services list. Terraform extends the same work to repeatable, reviewable infrastructure definitions.
lessons.example: An organization must provision identical test environments regularly; Terraform makes the resource configuration repeatable and version-controlled.
lessons.pitfall: Always verify the active project and review infrastructure plans before applying.
lessons.lab: In your terminal run: gcloud config list ; gcloud run services list --region=us-east1 --project=cloud-tam-portfolio (read-only).

lessons.summary: Cloud Monitoring provides metrics, charts and alerts; Cloud Logging records and searches logs. Audit logs can show who changed resources.
terms: Error Reporting helps aggregate application exceptions
lessons.connection: Map Cloud Monitoring to IBM Instana observability and your Akamai/Prolexic operational incident workflows: metrics expose symptoms; logs help explain causes.
lessons.example: A new Cloud Run revision begins returning HTTP 500 errors. Inspect revision traffic, service logs and metrics, then roll traffic back when appropriate.
lessons.pitfall: No single metric proves root cause. Correlate deployment changes, logs, latency and dependency health.
lessons.lab: Console → Logging → Logs Explorer. Filter by your existing Cloud Run service and check request status or application errors.

lessons.t: Cloud Run operations, revisions and scaling
lessons.summary: Cloud Run revisions are immutable deployment versions. Traffic can be shifted between revisions. Autoscaling is influenced by requests, concurrency and configured limits.
terms: Traffic splitting = gradual rollout or rollback
min instances may reduce cold-start impact and incur cost
lessons.connection: Your Cloud Run deployments produced new revisions. This is how a TAM can investigate a bad deployment without immediately rebuilding the whole application.
lessons.example: A revision causes new errors. Route traffic back to a known-good revision while investigating.
lessons.pitfall: Deleting a service is not the same as moving traffic off a faulty revision.
lessons.lab: Console → Cloud Run → existing service → Revisions / Traffic. Inspect allocation; do not modify your production app during study.

lessons.summary: GKE operates Kubernetes clusters. A Pod runs containers, a Deployment manages replica sets, and a Service provides stable access to Pods. Autopilot reduces node administration.
lessons.connection: Think of Kubernetes as orchestration for many service components across nodes; your historical escalation coordination across network, application and infrastructure teams maps to its layers.
lessons.example: A containerized platform requires fine-grained Kubernetes configuration across many microservices. GKE is often appropriate.
lessons.pitfall: A Kubernetes Service and Google Cloud Run service are not the same object.
lessons.lab: Read-only: explore GKE cluster and workload menus. No cluster required; clusters can incur charges.

lessons.summary: Snapshots protect disks; images help recreate VMs; regional design can improve resilience. RPO is tolerable data loss and RTO is tolerable recovery time.
lessons.connection: Link this to incident response and service recovery for large enterprise customers you supported: restoring service and restoring lost data are separate objectives.
lessons.example: If a workload tolerates 15 minutes of data loss, its backup/replication design must meet that RPO.
lessons.pitfall: A snapshot is not an automatically tested full disaster-recovery strategy.
lessons.lab: Compute Engine → Snapshots; inspect schedules and retention options without making new resources.

lessons.t: Cloud DNS, load balancing and connectivity
lessons.summary: Cloud DNS manages DNS zones; Cloud Load Balancing distributes incoming traffic; Cloud VPN and Interconnect connect other networks with Google Cloud.
lessons.connection: Your BlueCat DNS/DDI and Akamai edge networking knowledge translates directly. Separate name resolution, network reachability, frontend routing and application health during troubleshooting.
lessons.example: A public site returns a timeout: investigate DNS answer, load-balancer health, firewall reachability, backend availability and application logs.
lessons.pitfall: A successful DNS lookup does not establish application reachability.
lessons.lab: Console → Network services → Load balancing / Cloud DNS. Identify which layer each service operates at.

lessons.summary: Quotas constrain resource usage; budgets help detect spend; labels support organization and cost allocation. Different resources carry different billing implications.
lessons.connection: Translate enterprise change control and customer account health to cloud operations: check quotas, resource ownership, cost surprises and unused testing services.
lessons.example: A deployment fails with RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED: inspect the applicable project/region quota before changing architecture.
lessons.pitfall: A quota increase is not always immediate, and a quota is not a billing budget.
lessons.lab: Console → IAM & Admin → Quotas & System Limits. Browse only.

questions.q: A team wants production resources isolated from development, with separate IAM permissions and cost visibility. What is the best starting approach?
o: Use a single bucket for everything
questions.why: Projects provide resource, API, IAM and cost-tracking boundaries. Assign roles and budgets for each project.

questions.q: A Cloud Run application needs to read from Firestore. Which approach best follows least privilege?
o: Grant the project Editor role to all users
Attach a dedicated service account with required Firestore permissions
Generate a permanent Owner key inside source code
questions.why: Use a workload service account with only the necessary resource access; avoid broad roles and long-lived static keys.

questions.q: You need to deploy a stateless containerized HTTP API with unpredictable demand and minimal server management. Choose a service.
o: Compute Engine VM with manual scaling
questions.why: Cloud Run is designed for managed application and container deployment and automatic scaling.

questions.q: A VM has only a private IP but must fetch software updates from the internet. What can provide outbound internet connectivity?
questions.why: Cloud NAT allows eligible instances without external IPs to initiate outbound connections; suitable routes are still required.

questions.q: Azar Tree Services stores flexible quote records as documents. Which database most closely matches this model?
questions.why: Firestore provides a managed document data model used for application records.

questions.q: Before making Terraform infrastructure changes, which command previews proposed modifications?
questions.why: terraform plan shows proposed changes; terraform apply attempts to enact them.

questions.q: Users report HTTP 500 errors immediately after a new Cloud Run deployment. What should you inspect first?
o: Cloud Run revision metrics/logs and recent traffic changes
Only IAM roles of unrelated projects
questions.why: A deployment-correlated failure calls for checking the new revision, requests, errors, dependencies and traffic.

questions.q: A Cloud Run deployment is unhealthy. How can you restore traffic quickly if an earlier revision is healthy?
o: Route traffic back to the healthy revision
questions.why: Cloud Run supports revision-based traffic management for rollback and staged rollout.

questions.q: In Kubernetes, which resource commonly maintains the desired number of stateless application Pods?
questions.why: A Deployment manages replica sets and Pod rollout state.

questions.q: A service has RPO of 15 minutes. What does that mean?
o: Data loss should not exceed about 15 minutes
Every VM is deleted after 15 minutes
questions.why: RPO is the maximum acceptable amount of lost data measured in time, not restoration duration.

questions.q: A hostname resolves, but users cannot connect to the application. What is the most appropriate next approach?
o: Check backend health, load balancer, firewall and application connectivity
questions.why: DNS resolution proves name-to-address mapping worked, not end-to-end connectivity.

questions.q: A deployment is blocked by a regional CPU quota limit. What should you check?
questions.why: CPU quotas are subject to project/region limits; assess usage, quota increases or alternative capacity.

questions.q: Which role category is generally preferable to broad primitive/basic Editor for a specific task?
questions.why: Predefined task-specific roles typically narrow privileges compared with Editor.

questions.q: A data analyst needs to query several terabytes of event data using SQL for reporting. Which product is a strong fit?
questions.why: BigQuery is a managed analytics data warehouse suited to large analytical datasets.

questions.q: In Google Cloud VPC networking, a VPC network is generally ___ while its subnets are ___.
questions.why: GCP VPC networks are global resources; subnets live in regions.

questions.q: A TAM wants an alert when an application latency metric exceeds a threshold. Which GCP product?
questions.why: Cloud Monitoring provides time-series metrics and alerting policies.

questions.q: Which command lists existing Cloud Run services in a specified region?
questions.why: gcloud run services list is a read-only inventory operation, and --region narrows the location.

questions.q: An organization wants Kubernetes but less responsibility managing cluster nodes. Which GKE mode is designed for this?
questions.why: GKE Autopilot reduces infrastructure and node-management overhead.

questions.q: Which statement best distinguishes a snapshot from a VM image?
o: Snapshots are disk point-in-time backups; images are reusable disk templates
Snapshots always replace databases; images are DNS records
Images are always cheaper than snapshots
questions.why: Snapshots preserve disk state and images are used to create/boot new VM disks.

questions.q: A scheduled Cloud Scheduler job must invoke a private Cloud Run service. What is an appropriate design?
o: Use an authenticated service account with permission to invoke the service
Embed an Owner key in the URL
questions.why: A service identity with Cloud Run invocation permissions enables authenticated calls without making the service public.

questions.q: A legacy application needs specific OS packages and direct SSH access for administration. Which compute product fits best?
questions.why: Compute Engine offers direct VM and operating-system control.

questions.q: Which logs are especially useful for investigating who modified IAM policy?
questions.why: Cloud Audit Logs help identify resource administration and access events.

questions.q: An app needs a relational database supporting ordinary SQL transactions. Which service is a likely fit?
questions.why: Cloud SQL manages common relational database engines.

questions.q: A GCP billing budget reaches 100%. What happens by default?
o: A configured alert can notify recipients; spending is not automatically blocked
questions.why: A budget is a monitoring and alerting tool, not a default hard spending cap.

questions.q: A company needs an encrypted site-to-site connection between an on-premises network and a Google Cloud VPC. Which service?
questions.why: Cloud VPN provides IPsec tunnels between networks.

questions.q: Your team needs a gradual deployment to only a fraction of production traffic. What Cloud Run capability helps?
questions.why: Traffic splitting allows staged rollout percentages across revisions.

questions.q: How should applications generally access Google Cloud APIs from a supported Google Cloud workload?
o: Use its attached service account and short-lived credentials
Put a permanent Owner key in GitHub
questions.why: Workload identities and managed credentials reduce static-key exposure.

questions.q: Which tool is normally used to inspect Kubernetes Pods?
questions.why: kubectl get pods displays Pods in the selected Kubernetes context and namespace.

questions.q: A team wants to reduce potential downtime across zones for a critical service. What principle matters most?
o: Use a single disk snapshot as failover
questions.why: High availability needs redundant placement, appropriate load balancing and failure handling.

questions.q: What does a project quota primarily limit?
o: Consumption of particular cloud resources or API usage
The number of labels in a study plan only
The length of an IAM role name
questions.why: Quotas control specific resource usage/rates, not total spend directly.

questions.q: A team builds a Docker image and needs GKE to deploy it in 2026. Where should the container image be stored?
questions.why: Artifact Registry is the recommended image repository; Container Registry was shut down in 2025. Adapted from Module 4; checked against current service guidance.

questions.q: A GKE frontend must reach backend Pods even as those Pods are restarted and given new IP addresses. What should the team create?
o: A Kubernetes Service for the backend
Static external IP on each Pod
A separate VPC for each Pod
questions.why: A Kubernetes Service exposes a stable endpoint to a changing set of backend Pods. Adapted from Module 7; checked against current service guidance.

questions.q: A stateful GKE workload needs stable identities and predictable Pod hostnames after rescheduling. Which Kubernetes resource is designed for this?
questions.why: StatefulSets maintain stable Pod network identity and ordered identity across rescheduling. Adapted from Module 7; checked against current service guidance.

questions.q: A container image is ready in Artifact Registry and you need to run it on GKE. What is the normal next step?
o: Reference the image in a Kubernetes Deployment manifest and apply it using kubectl
Copy the image to Cloud Storage and point Pods at the bucket
Install Docker on every user workstation
questions.why: Kubernetes Deployment definitions reference container images; kubectl applies the desired state. Adapted from Module 4; checked against current service guidance.

questions.q: Your Compute Engine app writes logs to local files. What is the current recommended way to ingest these and VM metrics into Google Cloud Observability?
o: Configure Ops Agent on the VM
Install legacy Stackdriver Logging Agent as a new standard
Rely on serial console for all application logs
questions.why: Ops Agent is the recommended agent for Compute Engine logs and metrics; legacy agents ended regular maintenance in September 2026. Adapted from Module 3; checked against current service guidance.

questions.q: You need one Cloud Monitoring dashboard showing metrics from projects A, B and C. What do you configure?
o: A metrics scope that includes A, B and C
questions.why: A metrics scope in a scoping project allows dashboards and alert policies to see multiple monitored projects. Adapted from Modules 1 and 5; checked against current service guidance.

questions.q: A VM CPU metric crosses 90 percent. The team needs an email notification without custom scripts. What should you configure?
o: Cloud Monitoring alerting policy and email notification channel
Cloud Logging export to a local CSV
questions.why: Cloud Monitoring alerting policies evaluate metrics and notification channels deliver email. Adapted from Module 3; checked against current service guidance.

questions.q: A distributed request crosses four microservices. You need to identify where the latency occurs. Which approach works?
o: Distributed tracing using Cloud Trace instrumentation
Only average VM CPU in Monitoring
questions.why: Cloud Trace provides per-span timings to help locate slow segments in a distributed request. Adapted from Module 6; checked against current service guidance.

questions.q: Your team wants to review infrastructure changes before applying them to Google Cloud. Which 2026 workflow is appropriate?
o: Terraform configuration in version control, review a plan, then apply using approved automation or Infrastructure Manager
Create a new Deployment Manager deployment
Make production changes manually before review
Store command screenshots in Cloud Storage
questions.why: Deployment Manager support ended in April 2026; use Terraform-based infrastructure as code and review changes before applying. Adapted from Modules 1 and 4; checked against current service guidance.

questions.q: A new production Compute Engine VM will be created in a project that does not yet exist. What is the correct order?
o: Create project, link billing as needed, enable Compute Engine API, create VM
Create the VM then use --project to create a project
Enable API in another project and skip project creation
Create a VM from the billing report
questions.why: Resources need a project. Enable the relevant API in the target project and ensure required billing and IAM are configured. Adapted from Module 2; checked against current service guidance.

questions.q: An external auditor must read project resources, but organization policy restricts identities to the company domain. What should you do?
o: Use an approved identity in the permitted domain and grant minimal read-only access
Grant broad Owner access to any consumer Gmail address
Publish project credentials in a document
questions.why: Domain restricted sharing must be respected; approved identity and least privilege are the core controls. Adapted from Module 2; checked against current service guidance.

questions.q: A workload in project A must read a BigQuery dataset in project B. Which access is needed?
o: Grant the workload identity dataset read access in B and query job permissions where the jobs run
Make both projects Owners of each other
Put a service account JSON key in source code
Grant Viewer on project A only
questions.why: BigQuery data access and permissions to create query jobs are separate; the service account needs permissions scoped to each operation. Adapted from Module 2; checked against current service guidance.

questions.q: VMs need to read BigQuery data in another project. Which identity approach follows modern guidance?
o: Attach a service account to the VM and grant the needed cross-project IAM permissions
Download a permanent service-account key into VM metadata
Share a human user password across VMs
Grant project-wide Owner to all users
questions.why: Prefer attached service accounts and short-lived credentials, with least-privilege IAM in the data project. Adapted from Modules 2 and 4; checked against current service guidance.

questions.q: VMs have only internal IP addresses but must call Google Cloud Storage APIs. What subnet feature permits this without requiring external VM IPs?
o: A public IP on each VM
questions.why: Private Google Access enables qualifying VM instances without external IPs to reach Google APIs/services; review DNS/routing and organizational restrictions. Adapted from Module 7; checked against current service guidance.

questions.q: An internet-facing TCP application requires preservation of original client IP addresses at the backend. Which load balancer family is most relevant?
o: External proxy Network Load Balancer without proxy protocol
questions.why: Passthrough network load balancing preserves client source IP information at backend VMs; proxy load balancers terminate and create a new connection. Adapted from Module 7; checked against current service guidance.

questions.q: You store Cloud Storage objects and want them to transition to Coldline after 90 days and be deleted 365 days after creation. What is the simplest approach?
o: Object Lifecycle Management with SetStorageClass at age 90 and Delete at age 365
Use a Pub/Sub subscription without any processor
questions.why: Object lifecycle rules apply age since object creation and can transition storage class or delete at specified ages. Adapted from Module 4; checked against current service guidance.

questions.q: You need to retain 60 days of BigQuery event logs and automatically remove older data while keeping the table. What should you use?
o: Time-partitioned table with a 60-day partition expiration
Set the entire table expiration to 60 days
Assume BigQuery deletes old rows automatically
questions.why: Partition expiration removes old partitions while retaining newer partitions and the table. Adapted from Module 7; checked against current service guidance.

questions.q: Sensors send high-volume time-series readings and need low-latency key-based access. Which managed database is a common fit?
o: Cloud SQL for every streaming sensor by default
A Cloud Storage bucket with one object per reading
questions.why: Bigtable is designed for high-throughput, low-latency wide-column access patterns, including time-series data. Adapted from Module 6; checked against current service guidance.

questions.q: A company has globally distributed transactional relational data and needs horizontal scaling. Which service is designed for it?
questions.why: Spanner supports relational SQL and strong transactional consistency with distributed scale. Adapted from Module 7; checked against current service guidance.

questions.q: You need to estimate BigQuery on-demand query costs before executing a large SELECT. What should you do?
o: Perform a dry run and use estimated bytes processed for pricing
Estimate based only on result row count
Make a new VM to count rows
questions.why: BigQuery dry runs estimate bytes processed without executing the query; actual cost also depends on current pricing and other factors. Adapted from Module 4; checked against current service guidance.

questions.q: A security team wants to analyze logs from multiple projects in BigQuery for 60 days. What is a managed collection approach?
o: Use an appropriate aggregated Cloud Logging sink to BigQuery and configure retention in the destination
Install a custom cron job only
Use metrics scope to move logs into BigQuery
questions.why: Cloud Logging sinks route matching log entries to a BigQuery dataset; metrics scopes are for monitoring metrics, not automatic log export. Adapted from Module 2; checked against current service guidance.

questions.q: Finance needs to analyze costs for several billing accounts with SQL and a dashboard. What is appropriate?
o: Export Cloud Billing data to BigQuery and visualize it in Looker Studio
Use the pricing calculator as a record of actual costs
questions.why: Billing exports provide actual cost detail; BigQuery and Looker Studio support SQL analysis and dashboards. Adapted from Modules 1 and 4; checked against current service guidance.

questions.q: You want a GKE workload to run with reduced node-management overhead. Which cluster mode should you evaluate?
o: A fixed standalone VM with no orchestration
questions.why: GKE Autopilot manages much of cluster infrastructure and workload placement, but pricing must still be evaluated against workload needs. Adapted from Module 7; checked against current service guidance.

questions.q: An operations team needs audited SSH access to Compute Engine Linux VMs. Which feature integrates sign-in with IAM?
o: OS Login with appropriate IAM roles
A single shared SSH private key
Make each VM public and grant Owner
questions.why: OS Login integrates OS access with Google Cloud IAM and supports centralized access administration. Adapted from Module 5; checked against current service guidance.
